name: Sosaku-hanga creative print
summary: The artist draws, cuts and prints the block alone, and so rejects the three trades of the ukiyo-e shop. The result is a bold cut, an individual block, abstract shape and visible tool marks.

philosophy.core_thesis: A print is art when one person makes the whole of it, from the drawing to the last rub of the baren.
design_principles: Cut the block yourself. Leave the gouge and knife marks in the print.
Use 1–8 inks, and choose them with the cut: a large black mass, a field of red, a ground of blue-grey.
Use the grain of the plank or the plywood as a texture, not a fault.
Print the ink unevenly, 0.5–1.5 mm out of register in places, and keep the shift.
Allow abstract shape, or a strong, simple figure, with no soft gradation.
Sign in pencil in the margin, and write the edition number (for example 12/30).
Print on washi or on thin machine paper with a baren or a small press.
anti_patterns: A polished, even gradation in the manner of a commercial print
A carver and a printer who are not the artist
Pretty detail with no cut mark

process.matrix: A plank, plywood or sometimes linoleum, cut by the artist with a knife and gouges.
process.press: A baren or a spoon by hand, or a small press.
process.image_making: One artist draws, cuts and prints. No publisher sets the subject.

inks.strategy: Water-based or oil-based ink, 1–8 passes, mixed by the artist. The black block prints the mass, and the colour blocks print on or beside it.

screening.rule: Make a tone with a flat mass of ink or a field of cut lines. The style has no screen.

registration.rule: Allow 0.5–1.5 mm of shift between the inks, and keep it as the sign of the hand.

substrate.stock: Washi, or a thin machine-made paper.
substrate.finish: Soft and absorbent, with no coating.

surface.impression: Light to medium. A hard rub leaves the line of the block on the back.
surface.sheen: Matt, with a slight shine where the ink is thick.
surface.texture: Visible wood grain, gouge marks, and ink that is thick in one place and thin in another.

marks: gouge and knife marks left visible
pencil signature and edition number in the margin

evidence.title: Fisherman
evidence.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access

emotion.target_response: The force of one hand: the viewer feels that a person cut this block, and that the person had something to say.

use_cases: editorial art with a personal voice
avoid_when: The brief needs a soft, polished Edo or shin-hanga finish.
The message needs exact register and a clean, regular edge.

modifiers.how: Add tonal blocks and wiped gradations, keep a thin key line, and bring the register to 0.2 mm.
Cut deeper, use black and one raw colour, and keep the wood grain.
